text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Sofia City Court declared state owned Balkanbank insolvent on the basis of a claim filed by the Bulgarian National Bank, a court official said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved a draft bill to restore to its original owners forest land collectivised under the communist rule. @
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it had asked the Sofia City Court to start liquidation proceedings against First Private Bank (FPB).

FPB shareholders decided to offer to Banque Nationale de Paris - London Investment Branch a 51 percent stake in FPB for $20 million and a pledge to repay $40 million of FPB debt to the Finance Ministry.

-- Shareholders of the private Bulgarian-Russian Investment Bank decided to introduce a two-tier management through executive and supervisory boards to comply with stricter management requirements under the new Banking law. @

-- Bulgaria's chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said he might ask the Constitutional Court whether parts of newly approved bill to open secret police files from the communist era contravened civil rights of Bulgarians.
-- Bulgaria's biggest state oil refinery Neftochim said it would cut 10 percent of its staff in line with government's policy to cut spending.
-- Bulgaria expects some 70,000 tonnes of tobacco from this year's crop, an Agriculture ministry official said.

-- Bulgarian grain producers said they had asked the cabinet to change state quality requirements for bread wheat as late summer and rainfalls in the past weeks have seriously affected the crop in Bulgaria's northeast main production regions. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
